text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Eighteen major uranium deposits have been identified by the Federal Government as prospective sites for new mines that could take advantage of the world's currently high uranium prices. Four deposits are earmarked for short-term development, requiring total investments of around A$625 million. Page 1.

Telecommunications planning powers may be given to the states and local government in a new federal government push to change the industry before it is opened to new investment next year. The industry fears such moves could jeopardise next year's competition by discouraging new investments. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday spoke out in Parliament against "anyone" who wanted to return Australia to "anything approaching the White Australia policy". His action came after Malaysian, Indonesian and Australian business representatves added their voices to a race debate that was getting out of control. Page 1.

The Federal Opposition has once again asked Prime Minister John Howard to fire Industry Minister John Moore for breaching the ministerial guidelines on the ownership of shares. Opposition Industry spokesman Simon Crean said Moore had engaged in share trading with the company Ralsten Pty Ltd. Page 1.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's political parties yesterday joined forces to support a parliamentary motion opposing racial discrimination and re-affirming support for a non-discriminatory immigration policy. The government was concerned about the potential damage the local debate on immigration was having on Australia's economic and trade interests. Prime Minister Howard said the motion was designed to "send a clear and unambiguous signal, particularly to the nations of our region". Page 1.

As Queensland's Government came under pressure to act following the shock resignation of Ken Carruthers QC from the CJC inquiry into electoral bribery, Premier Rob Borbidge, in a statement to Parliament, said the resignation was "unjustified" and refuted Curruthers' claims of political interference, describing the remarks as "offensive". The Queensland government has demanded the retired judge repay A$350,000 in fees. Page 1.

Independent MP Pauline Hanson, the woman who triggered the debate on immigration policies and funding for Aborigines, was notably absent yesterday when Parliament received a motion which was specifically aimed at replying to her arguments. In her absence, the only voice speaking out against the motion was West Australian Independent MP Graeme Campbell. Page 1.

According to a state government report into Victoria's child protection system, 100 children known to protective services have died over the past several years and from that figure, at least 16 children have died from abuse. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Both houses of federal parliament and both sides of politics joined yesterday to pass a historic motion aimed at taking the sting out of the racism debate. The motion, backed by Prime Minister John Howard and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley, strongly backed multiculturalism, non-discriminatory immigration policies and Aboriginal reconciliation. Pauline Hanson, the controversial MP whose maiden parliamentary speech sparked the controversy, refused to take part in the debate, opting instead to spend the day in Melbourne. Page 1.

In the shadow of the federal government attacking Australian executives' salaries and calling for wage restraint, it has been revealed that the salaries of the Treasury's top executives have doubled in the last year. The number of officials on A$100,000-plus increased from 15 to 39 during 1995/96. Page 1.

Federal Opposition Industry spokesman Simon Crean has accused Industry Minister John Moore of active share market trading in flagrant breach of Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines. When questioned by Crean in Parliament, Moore refused to confirm or deny that Ralsten Pty Ltd, a company in which he owns shares, had sold mining shares. Page 1.

Although it is likely to narrowly avert a no confidence motion following the shock resignation of Ken Carruthers QC from the CJC inquiry into electoral bribery, the Queensland Government is facing major political fallout from the resignation. Continuing is attack on Carruthers, State Premier Rob Borbidge demanded in Parliament yesterday that he repay A$400,000 he recieved in fees during the inquiry. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Victorian Government yesterday unveiled plans to build a 52,000-seat "hi-tech" stadium to be situated behind Spencer Street rail yards and given the title Victoria Stadium. The A$200 million dollar stadium will be used for AFL football, soccer rugby and general entertainment. Page A1.

Both major Australian political parties got together yesterday to head off the race debate in a joint statement denouncing racial intolerance and reaffirming support for a non-discriminatory immigration policy and Aboriginal reconciliation. The speeches had the overwhelming support of the Federal Parliament. Page A1.

Victoria's child-protection system came under renewed attack yesterday with the revelation of the deaths of four State wards in the new Victorian Child Death Review Committee's annual report. The report also revealed that since 1989, 100 children in Statecare had died. Page A1.

Melbourne's Roman Catholic Archbishop George Pell yesterday publicly apologised to all victims of sexual abuse by clergy, offering free counselling and compensation of up to A$50,000 for each victim. Compensation payments will be ex gratia, meaning no leal liability is admitted. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
